goal: Introduce four distinct roles that gate platform surface access and write permissions so each user only operates within their functional boundary.
success_metrics: Scoped users cannot access surfaces outside their role boundary via UI or direct URL
Full Access admins can assign and change roles without friction during invite and from User Management
Role changes take effect immediately without delayed sync
constraints: Only Full Access admins can invite users, assign roles, and access User Management
Role enforcement must be at both UI and API layers — no client-only gating
Last Full Access admin cannot downgrade their own role
Role changes must be recorded in the audit log
assumptions: Scoped managers (AEP, Training & Simulations) have no cross-surface dashboard visibility
Dashboard Viewers see all dashboard data across surfaces (not scoped) — creates an inversion vs. functional managers
Training and Simulations access is intentionally bundled into one role
Role change takes effect on next page load or API call, not via forced logout
SSO/SCIM provisioning is out of scope for v1
Bulk role operations are not required in v1
gaps: Dashboard Viewer 'all dashboard views' contradicts scoped manager dashboard filtering — scope must be reconciled
Export permissions for Dashboard Viewer are undefined — export is a read action not a write action
Granular write permissions within a surface (delete, archive, remove assignment) are unspecified for scoped managers
SSO/SCIM provisioning not addressed — enterprise buyers will ask immediately
Bulk role assignment flow not specified
Audit log surface location in UI not described
No access request path for scoped users who need elevated permissions
No first-login onboarding state for scoped users to understand their access boundary
Pending invite state (role change before activation) not addressed
edge_cases: Full Access admin downgrades own role — prevented only if last Full Access; otherwise allowed
Role downgrade for active session user — takes effect on next page load, not immediately
Scoped user navigates to gated URL — permission-denied empty state, not 404
Role change while user has active write-capable surface open
User with pending invite (unactivated) — can role be changed before activation?
Organization with only Dashboard Viewers — no functional work possible
User Management table with 100+ users — filtering by role not specified
Deactivation of Full Access admin — another Full Access admin must exist first
AEP Manager views Dashboards — sees AEP-scoped data only, not org-wide risk
Role change API call fails mid-confirmation — error state not defined

critical_questions.question: Is Dashboard Viewer access to all dashboard views intentional — giving them broader data visibility than functional managers?
Can Dashboard Viewers export reports and data?
Does 'manage' for scoped roles include delete, or only create/edit/assign?
Is SCIM/IdP provisioning in scope for v1? If yes, what is the role attribute mapping schema?
Is the Training and Simulations bundle intentional, or should simulation-only access be a separate role?
Must Full Access downgrade trigger immediate session invalidation, or is next-page-load acceptable from a security standpoint?
Where does the audit log surface in the UI? Is it a dedicated admin surface or a sub-section of User Management?
Is bulk role-change in scope for v1, or is single-user change the only supported pattern?

design_risks: Dashboard Viewer vs. scoped manager data inversion will confuse admins assigning roles and may result in wrong role assignments
Hidden navigation (vs. disabled with tooltip) leaves new scoped users with no visibility into what they're missing — creates perceived setup errors
Dashboard Viewer default on invite is correct for least-privilege but may create a support burden when admins forget to change it
Permission-denied 'contact your admin' message dead-ends scoped users with no in-product access request path
Role downgrade without session invalidation allows a short window of unauthorized write access for destructive actions
teaching_notes: RBAC ships as UX: build a state matrix (role × surface × action type) as the first design artifact before opening Figma
Start from the existing User Management table — RBAC extends it with a role column, badge, and inline selector
Role badges should use Stillsuit DS v2 status badge component — confirm whether four new variants are needed before designing
Permission-denied state should use the standard Stillsuit DS v2 empty-state pattern with a consistent message structure
Audit log may be a net-new surface — check for existing activity log patterns in campaign history or elsewhere
API-layer enforcement (403 responses) is a backend concern — confirm Eng ownership before designing UI that assumes it
